description: >
  Measure whether an ellmer agent uses accepted, corrected, withdrawn,
  instruction-like, and host-denied memory properly with a credential-free
  vitals::Task.
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Evaluate agent recall of reviewed memory}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

An agent can call a memory tool and still answer from the wrong revision, treat
retained text as instructions, or invent an answer when the host has withdrawn
access. This article provides a small, credential-free `vitals::Task` for
measuring those behaviors with synthetic local Graft stores.

The evaluation covers accepted, corrected, missing, withdrawn,
instruction-like, and host-denied memory. The scripted solver makes a real
ellmer tool request and executes the real `graft_tool()` result. Only the
provider response is scripted locally, so the ordinary package test suite does
not need an API key or make a network request.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
has_recall_eval <- requireNamespace("vitals", quietly = TRUE) &&
  packageVersion("vitals") >= "0.4.0" &&
  requireNamespace("httr2", quietly = TRUE)
if (has_recall_eval) {
  eval_helpers <- system.file(
    "evals",
    "recall-evaluation.R",
    package = "graft",
    mustWork = TRUE
  )
  source(eval_helpers)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = has_recall_eval
)
```

If `vitals` 0.4 or `httr2` is unavailable, the code examples remain visible
but are not evaluated while building the package website. Install the released
versions before running the evaluation locally.

The installed package exposes the self-contained fixture and task helpers at a
stable path:

```{r load-helper, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file(
  "evals",
  "recall-evaluation.R",
  package = "graft",
  mustWork = TRUE
))
```

## Run the offline task

The fixture creates one local store per case. Every accepted store contains a
reviewed note and its source; the correction and withdrawal are recorded as
distinct decision events. The denied case retains the note but the host
callback returns `FALSE`.

```{r fixture}
fixture <- graft_recall_eval_fixture()
names(fixture$cases)
```

The solver uses a deliberately narrow response convention so answer scoring
does not mistake a contradiction for a correct answer. A model returns only
the reviewed value, preserving units when present, or one of the two
abstention tokens: `NO_REVIEWED_ANSWER` and
`NO_REVIEWED_MEMORY_ACCESS`. Punctuation and case are normalized, but extra
claims are not accepted.

```{r run-task}
task <- graft_recall_eval_task(fixture)
task$eval(view = FALSE)
samples <- task$get_samples()
samples[, c("case", "result", "score")]
```

The scripted task exercises the complete ellmer turn sequence. For example,
the first case contains both a tool request and the tool result that Graft
returned:

```{r inspect-turns}
paste(
  vapply(
    samples$solver_chat[[1]]$get_turns(),
    function(turn) paste(format(turn), collapse = "\n"),
    character(1)
  ),
  collapse = "\n\n"
)
```

## Read the two scoring dimensions

`score` is correct only when both dimensions pass. The scorer also logs them
separately in `scorer_metadata`, so a wrong answer from a valid current note is
not confused with a right-looking answer that had no reviewed support.

```{r score-dimensions}
score_table <- data.frame(
  case = samples$case,
  answer_quality = vapply(
    samples$scorer_metadata,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "answer_quality"
  ),
  evidence_integrity = vapply(
    samples$scorer_metadata,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "evidence_integrity"
  ),
  observed_evidence_status = vapply(
    samples$scorer_metadata,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "observed_evidence_status"
  ),
  failure = vapply(
    samples$scorer_metadata,
    `[[`,
    character(1),
    "failure"
  )
)
score_table
```

For accepted rows, the evidence check compares the tool result with the exact
decision, selection, root reference, source reference, and retained bytes in
the synthetic fixture. For missing and withdrawn rows, it requires the tool to
return no content. For the denied row, it requires the eligibility error and no
retained content. The scorer reads the request and its linked result directly from the recorded
`solver_chat`.

## Read the vitals log

`Task$log()` writes the Inspect-compatible evaluation record. `vitals 0.4`
can read that record back into a tibble, including the recorded solver chats.

```{r read-log}
log_path <- task$log()
logged <- vitals::vitals_log_read(
  log_path,
  solver_chat = samples$solver_chat[[1]]
)
logged[, c("input", "result", "score")]
```

The offline log records real tool calls with scripted answers. Keep it with
the fixture inputs when comparing runs.

## Run a chosen model

Supply a fresh ellmer chat to run the same cases and scoring rules against a
model. With your provider credentials configured, set `GRAFT_RECALL_EVAL_MODEL`
to the model you want to evaluate. This example uses an OpenAI chat. Other
ellmer providers can supply the chat in the same way.

```{r live, eval=FALSE}
model <- Sys.getenv("GRAFT_RECALL_EVAL_MODEL")
stopifnot(nzchar(model))
live <- graft_recall_eval_task(
  fixture,
  chat = ellmer::chat_openai(model = model),
  log_dir = file.path(getwd(), "recall-evaluation-live")
)
live$eval(view = FALSE)
live$get_samples()[, c("case", "result", "score")]
```

Each case uses its own chat and store. Inspect the linked recall request and
result alongside the answer when interpreting a model's score.

## Pair vitals with scans

Use `vitals` to score *whether* the agent got the right answer and obeyed
withdrawal or access boundaries. Use [scans](https://github.com/JamesHWade/scans)
to investigate *how* a run unfolded across tool calls and turns: every
`graft_tool()` and `graft_tools()` result carries a plain-data `@extra$graft`
record on its `ContentToolResult` (`status`, `stream`, `decision_id`,
`selection_id`, `artifact_refs`, `truncated`, `omitted_count`) so recorded
`solver_chat` objects retain machine-readable consultation metadata with no
live store handles.
